compiler: Ranked: CUDA 12.8.93, nvcc -O3 -DQSB_ZEROS_N=24 -o pinning pinning.cu -lcrypto -lm; no local nvcc
added_multiply_reap_and_fused_x3: QSB_MUL_REAP / QSB_X3_DBL2 / QSB_X3_TAIL in GPUMath.h: three independently switched, provably exact rewrites of the two per-addition sites this tree's lane program never reached. QSB_MUL_REAP reaps the ninth-word carry capture of the live short-carry field multiply, the last of the four live reductions that still emitted 'addc.u32 f8, 0, 0' between its two 977 fold chains and seeded z8 from it; the square, the short-carry square and the fused square-add-subtract all reaped theirs under QSB_RP_SQR, QSB_SQL_REAP and QSB_SAS_Z89_REAP. Bound: the even fold is L + 977*(x8,x10,x12,x14) with L < 2^256 and each addend below 977*2^32 < 2^42 at lanes 0..3, so the added mass is under 2^234 and lane 3 carries out only when L >= 2^256 - 2^234, at most 2^-22 per multiply -- the same event class and the same rate as the ninth-word reap and the FOLD65 arms this build already ships behind the host publication gate, and such an event only perturbs one candidate by 2^256 mod p, which the OpenSSL gate in pinning.cu rejects before publication. The multiply runs ten times per point addition. QSB_X3_DBL2 builds the doubled subtrahend of the fused X3 = a + b - 2c (the XYZZ addition's abscissa combiner) as four carry-ordered 64-bit self-adds plus one carry capture instead of four shifts, three right shifts, three ors and a top shift: 2c in radix 2^64 is c+c, lane i is (c_i<<1) plus the carry c_{i-1}>>63, a lane can never re-overflow because (c_i<<1) is even, and the capture is bit 256 of 2c, i.e. c3>>63 -- bit for bit the funnel form's five words at five instructions instead of eleven, the doubling QSB_SAS_Q2LANE already proves on the fused square. QSB_X3_TAIL ends that routine's fold correction where QSB_SHORT_CARRY ends every other correction in this file: the fold adds k = t4*K with t4 <= 3, so k < 2^33.6, and the carry reaches limb 2 only when t0 lies within 2^33.6 of 2^64 and t1 is 2^64-1, at most 2^-94.4 per addition -- below the 2^-95 the short-carry _ModSub256 and _ModAddLazy arms declare and far below the 2^-30 window QSB_C31 ships. Each arm restores its prior text byte for byte at 0; QSB_MUL_REAP is #error-gated on QSB_RP_SQR and QSB_SHORT_CARRY (transitively on QSB_HOST_GATE in pinning.cu) and QSB_X3_TAIL on QSB_SHORT_CARRY.
added_top_fold_word_form: QSB_MUL_FOLD65 / QSB_SQL_FOLD65 / QSB_SAS_FOLD65 in GPUMath.h: three independently switched rewrites of the lane top fold at the three live reductions (the field multiply, the short-carry plain square, the fused square-add-subtract). The lane forms this tree carries add z8*(2^32+977) as a 65-bit quantity -- a 64-bit low half into lane 0 and a one-bit high half that lane 1 receives through a captured carry -- and pay a zero-paired shift operand {zr,z8}, a carry-producing 64-bit add and a carry capture to build it. In words that low half is exactly { lo32(977*z8), hi32(977*z8) + z8 }, because 977*z8 < 2^42 leaves hi32(977*z8) < 2^10, and the 65th bit is the carry of that single 32-bit word add. Each arm emits the word form and drops that carry, so one 32-bit add replaces the paired operand, the carry-producing 64-bit add and the capture, while lane 1 still absorbs the carry out of lane 0 exactly as before and the lane-2 terminator remains whatever QSB_*_FOLDT2 selects. The two forms differ only when z8*(2^32+977) reaches 2^64, i.e. when the quotient limb is at least 2^32-977: at most 977/2^32 = 2^-22.04 per reduction for a uniformly distributed ninth word, the same event class and the same rate as the QSB_RP_SQR ninth-word reap this build already ships behind the host publication gate, and far above the 2^-86 lane-2 step of the FOLDT2 arms. Such an event perturbs one candidate's abscissa by 2^64 mod p and cannot publish a wrong hit, because the host gate recovers and re-hashes every hit exactly before publication. The arms share no register, are inert wherever their lane fold is off, and restore the 65-bit pair byte for byte at 0.
added_fused_square_lane_stack: Three independently switched, provably exact rewrites of the fused square-add-subtract _ModSqrAddSub2 in GPUMath.h, the routine every XYZZ addition on the ranked path calls for its abscissa. QSB_SAS_DBL64: the 512-bit cross-product sum is doubled in the eight 64-bit lanes it is packed into anyway, as one carry-propagating self-add chain (add.cc/addc.cc over d0..d7), instead of fifteen descending 32-bit funnel shifts. 2x in radix 2^64 is x+x with the carry out of lane i entering lane i+1, and that carry is exactly the bit the funnel chain moved across the corresponding word boundary, so all sixteen output words are identical; the carry out of lane 7 is bit 511 of the pre-doubled sum, precisely the bit the top funnel shift shf.l.wrap.b32 x15,x14,x15,1 discarded. Fifteen shifts and a strictly serial dependence chain become eight adds on the chain the diagonal squares already extend. QSB_SAS_FRD: the doubled-plus-diagonal accumulator already sits in the eight lanes the two 977 folds consume -- lanes 0..3 are the even fold's addend fr0..fr3 and lanes 4..7 the odd fold's h0..h3 -- so only the high half is split into 32-bit words, for the four 977 multiplies, and the low half's split together with both halves' repacks (twelve mov.b64 renames of the same bits) is dropped, retiring x0..x7 from the live set. QSB_SAS_Q2LANE: the doubled subtrahend of the lane accumulator is built from the 64-bit operand limbs as q+q -- four carry-ordered lane adds whose carry-out is bit 255 of q -- instead of one shift, seven funnel shifts, one shift and four word repacks; nt takes the same bit 255 that shr.u32 nt,q7,31 produced, the lane carries are the word carries the funnel form re-materialised, and the subtraction of 2q, the 3K correction and the 977 fold all see identical bits. The arm also retires the four operand-word splits of q. Each arm is independently restorable at its own name and QSB_SAS_Q2LANE is #error-gated on the lane accumulator it doubles into.
added_live_square_stack: Three independently switched, provably exact rewrites of the reduction tail of the *live* plain field square in GPUMath.h -- the QSB_SHORT_CARRY _ModSqr schedule, the routine every XYZZ doubling and both recovery squares call. The lane rewrites this tree already carries applied to the multiply and the fused square-add-subtract; the short-carry square still ran the carry-complete ninth and tenth words behind eight register splits and seven carry-ordered 32-bit adds. QSB_SQL_REAP drops the two ninth-word captures (f8, g8) and the tenth word z9: the even fold is L + 977*(x8,x10,x12,x14) with every addend limb below 977*2^32 < 2^42, so f8 and symmetrically g8 are nonzero only when that 320-bit chain passes 2^288 - 2^42, below 2^-95 per square for a uniformly distributed operand, and the only other path into z9 is a carry out of the w7 seed, which perturbs one candidate's x by a multiple of 2^256 mod p; the arm is #error-gated on QSB_RP_SQR, which pinning.cu gates on QSB_HOST_GATE, and that gate re-derives the public key and both hashes with OpenSSL before any hit is printed, so no false hit can be published -- the same trade the multiply and the fused square already take. The fold head then reads its quotient limb straight out of z8 and the 33-bit multiply-add collapses to the 32-bit one. QSB_SQL_LANE64 regroups the merge: the even fold already leaves f0..f3 as 64-bit registers and the odd fold enters one word up, so z1+=w0 .. z7+=w6 are exactly four 64-bit lane adds (lane 0 takes {0,w0}, lane i takes {w(2i-1),w(2i)}), w7 stays the ninth-word seed, every lane boundary is a word boundary of the same 288-bit sum, the carry into lane i+1 is the carry out of word 2i+1, and the four register splits of the even fold disappear. QSB_SQL_FOLD64 replaces the 32-bit top fold: with 2^256 == 2^32 + 977 (mod p) the fold adds z8*(2^32+977) < 2^64 + 2^42, whose low 64 bits are 977*z8 + (z8<<32) and whose 65th bit is that add's carry (set only for z8 >= 2^32-976), so lanes 0 and 1 take the pair and the residual carry dies in lane 2 -- word 5, two words above the word-3 terminator of the form it replaces, so the truncation is strictly later. All four lanes are then the output words and no recomposition is emitted. Each arm restores the schedule it replaces byte for byte at =0 (-DQSB_SQL_REAP=0, -DQSB_SQL_LANE64=0, -DQSB_SQL_FOLD64=0); LANE64 requires REAP and FOLD64 requires LANE64, both enforced with #error.
added_square_lane_stack: Two layered, independently switched, provably exact rewrites of the plain field square's reduction tail in GPUMath.h (_ModSqr, the QSB_SQR schedule), the routine the ranked XYZZ chain calls for every doubling and for both recovery squares. QSB_SQR_LANE64: the fold merge runs in 64-bit lanes. The even 977-fold already leaves f0..f3 as 64-bit registers and the odd fold enters one word up, so the eight carry-ordered 32-bit adds z1+=w0 .. z7+=w6 are exactly four 64-bit lane adds -- lane 0 takes {0,w0}, lane 1 {w1,w2}, lane 2 {w3,w4}, lane 3 {w5,w6} -- and w7 remains the ninth-word seed the reaped accumulator consumes. Every lane boundary is a word boundary of the same 288-bit sum and the carry into lane i+1 is precisely the carry out of word 2i+1, so all output bits are unchanged, while the four register recompositions of the even fold disappear with the word form. QSB_SQR_FOLD64: the top fold stays in those lanes. Because 2^256 == 2^32 + 977 (mod p) the fold adds z8*(2^32+977), a 65-bit quantity whose low 64 bits are 977*z8 + (z8<<32) and whose 65th bit is that add's carry; adding the low half at lane 0 and the carry at lane 1 leaves the result already in the four output lanes, so neither the recomposition nor the truncated 32-bit carry tail is emitted, and the residual carry now dies one whole lane later (words 4,5) than the tail it replaces, making the arm strictly tighter than the form on the crown. Each arm restores the previous text byte for byte when switched off, and the second refuses to compile without the first.
added_lane_stack: Three layered, independently switched, provably exact rewrites of the post-square tail of _ModSqrAddSub2 (GPUMath.h), the fused square-add-subtract that every XYZZ addition on the ranked path calls fifteen times per candidate. QSB_SAS_SPRE: the accumulator's three post-square addends collapse into one. The reaped accumulator {z8,z7..z0} is a Z/2^288 register, so adding e, adding the split-3p offset 3*2^256 and subtracting the doubled canonical q commute and associate, and every grouping truncates in exactly the same place (the carry or borrow out of z8). S = e + 3*2^256 - 2q is therefore assembled from the operand registers alone -- e is live as %8..%11 and q as %12..%15 at entry, so the whole assembly is off the square's dependent chain -- and one nine-word add chain replaces the eight-word e add with its top add, the nine-word 2q subtract with its top subtract, and their two carry terminators. QSB_SAS_LANE64: the same tail in 64-bit lanes. The even pseudo-Mersenne fold already leaves f0..f3 in 64-bit registers; the odd fold's eight words are re-paired one word up into four 64-bit lanes with w7 left as the ninth-word seed exactly as the reaped seed reads it, the precomputed addend is assembled in lanes directly from the operand pairs, and 3K = 0x300000b73 is one 64-bit immediate. Four carry-ordered 64-bit steps replace eight 32-bit ones in the fold merge and again in the addend application, the 3K borrow now propagates through word 3 instead of stopping at word 2, and only the two low lanes are ever split into halves. Lane arithmetic is the same base-2^64 positional form of the same 288-bit register: lane i holds words 2i and 2i+1 and the carry between lanes is the carry out of word 2i+1, so the bits are identical. QSB_SAS_FOLD64: the top fold in the same lanes. 2^256 == 2^32 + 977 mod p, so the fold adds z8*(2^32+977), a 65-bit value whose low 64 bits are 977*z8 + (z8<<32) and whose 65th bit is that add's carry; the pair goes in at lanes 0 and 1 and the carry dies in lane 2, one whole lane further than the 32-bit tail it replaces, and all four lanes are the output words with no recomposition. Each arm restores the text it replaced at 0 and is #error-gated on the arms it layers on.
added_this_submission: Three independently switched, provably exact rewrites of the two hottest per-candidate paths. QSB_SAS_Q2SHF (GPUMath.h, _ModSqrAddSub2): the fused square-add-subtract of the XYZZ addition subtracted the same canonical q twice through two carry-ordered eight-limb chains plus two top borrows; it now forms 2q exactly in nine words with nine funnel shifts of q (nt = q7>>31, n_i = (q_i<<1)|(q_{i-1}>>31), n0 = q0<<1) and subtracts it once. The nine-limb accumulator {z8,z7..z0} is a Z/2^288 register, so (z-q)-q and z-2q are the same residue and every downstream limb, the 3K subtraction and the 977 fold see identical bits; neither form borrows out of z8 because the accumulator stays above 2^256 until the 3K subtraction, the invariant the split-3p arm already maintains. Same instruction count, dependent borrow chain behind the square halved from eighteen to nine, and the shifts read only q, which is live before the column sums finish. QSB_D32_W63_BAL (sha_pinsha.cuh): the digest-32 block's last schedule word, whose only consumer is the folded round 63 that produces digest words 0 and 4, is paired as (s1(w13)+w8)+(w15+s0(w0)) instead of the left-to-right chain, cutting its dependent depth from three to two at the same three additions. QSB_TAILQ_W63_BAL (pinning.cu): the same pairing for the candidate tail block's W63, five terms including the constant-bank zero addend, depth four to two. Both reassociations are exact because addition mod 2^32 is associative and commutative, and the schedule word is bit-identical, so the two hashes and the recovered scalar are unchanged.
added_this_stack: Three further independently switched exact rewrites of the per-candidate SHA-256 compression, all in the ranked stage-0 path. QSB_TAILQ_ILV (pinning.cu): the live per-thread tail transform _SHA256TransformFastTail11Q produces each message-schedule word immediately before the round that consumes it instead of emitting three sixteen-word bursts ahead of three sixteen-round bursts; statement order and therefore every intra-group read is preserved and rounds never write w[], so the compression is bit-identical group for group while the schedule live range drops from sixteen words to the rolling recurrence window. QSB_RL_BAL0 (sha_pinsha.cuh): the ALU-add round becomes (h + KW) + (S1(e) + Ch) instead of a left-to-right chain, same term multiset, same three-input add folding. QSB_R63_KSPLIT (sha_pinsha.cuh): round 63's block-invariant K63 + F0 term is added to the a-slot word instead of to W63, and the two output pair sums are balanced, so the last schedule word is two adds from the digest word instead of three.
added_this_turn: Four independently switched exact rewrites carried into one submission. Three in the ranked stage-2 public-key tail (pinning.cu, kernel_pinning_pipeline stage 2): QSB_PK_TAIL_CONSTEXPR moves the generic double-hash epilogue into the discarded arm of an if-constexpr on the FAST_TAIL template argument, so its 32-byte digest buffer, 64-byte second block, sixteen-word block array and second digest state leave the ranked specialization before its frame is sized (the FAST_TAIL-false instantiation keeps the epilogue verbatim); QSB_PK_BLOCK9 then sizes the public-key message block to the nine words the specialized transform reads and nothing in that instantiation writes; QSB_PK_SLOPE_SEL selects the per-key slope by value rather than by array address so both four-limb slopes stay in registers across the rolled two-key body. One in the ranked gate's compression tail (sha_pinsha.cuh, _SHA256Pubkey33H0): QSB_RND_BAL2 keeps the folded round-63 constant off the schedule word's dependent path -- a + (K63 + IV0) is formed from round 62's output and a literal while w[15] is still reducing, and the gate word closes as ((a+K) + w[15]) + ((S1(f)+Ch) + (S0(b)+Maj)). The same nine 32-bit additions of the same nine terms are issued; addition mod 2^32 is associative and commutative, so the returned word is bit-identical and the dependent depth behind the last schedule word drops from four to three.
added_previous_submission: Two independently switched exact rewrites of the cofactor checkpoint and the recovery finish, ported from public submission 464fad51 (790,907,535 measured) onto this tree's named-level traversal. QSB_TREE_TOP16 (cofactor_checkpoint.h): the last sixteen subtree roots at products[2N-32..2N-17] merge their four up-sweep waves and three exclusion waves into four multiply waves that carry both roles -- eight pair products, then sixteen exclusions plus four quad products, then the extended exclusions plus two half roots, then the final exclusions plus the block root. The factor sets and the ((x * P2) * P4) * P8 association are the ones the down-sweep produces, so every excluded product and the root are bit-identical; the down-sweep resumes at count=32 with the register hand-off seeded from the merged wave's own outputs. QSB_FIN_ADD_LAZY (pinning.cu): the two sums in qsb_xyzz_finish_symmetric that feed only qsb_field_normalize and a _ModSub256/_ModMult pair (x_minus = F+H and the u+v rebuild) take _ModAddLazy -- the 2^256 carry folds as K and the conditional p-subtraction is skipped. The result stays in [0, 2^256) and congruent mod p; qsb_field_normalize maps [p, 2^256) to [0, K) exactly, and the only dropped case is a second carry after the K fold, a 2^-223-class event in the same exposure class QSB_C31 already ships. -DQSB_TREE_TOP16=0 restores the TOP2 top pair and the rolled exclusion waves; -DQSB_FIN_ADD_LAZY=0 restores the canonicalizing _ModAdd256 at both sites.

added_cross_sum_lane_merge: Three independently switched, provably exact regroupings of the 512-bit cross-product sum of the two hottest squares in GPUMath.h. QSB_SAS_XMERGE64 (_ModSqrAddSub2) and QSB_SQL_XMERGE64 (the live QSB_SHORT_CARRY _ModSqr) merge the even and odd column registers in the eight 64-bit lanes the sum is doubled in, instead of in sixteen 32-bit words that are then repacked: the even registers e2..e12 already span words 2..13 at lane alignment, the odd registers o1..o13 straddle lanes, so re-pairing their words one position up turns a fifteen-add 32-bit chain plus a sixteen-word pack into seven pairings and seven lane adds. Exact because lane i is words 2i and 2i+1 and the inter-lane carry is exactly the carry out of word 2i+1; the even chain's top register cannot overflow its lane (PP(5,7) plus one carry stays below 2^64 - 2^33), which is why the word form seeded x14 = x15 = 0, so word 14 holds the odd top plus the chain carry and word 15 stays zero. QSB_SQL_DBL64 doubles the live square's cross sum as eight 64-bit lane self-adds instead of fifteen descending funnel shifts (it is also the fallback arm of QSB_SQL_XMERGE64); both forms drop the bit above word 15, which is unreachable because 2*cross + diagonal is below 2^512. QSB_SQL_FRD keeps the live square's fold addends in the lanes the diagonal chain left them in -- fr0..fr3 are d0..d3, h0..h3 are d4..d7 -- so only the high four lanes are split into the words the 977 multiplies index. Each name restores the prior form byte for byte, and the QSB_SQL_ arms are #error-gated on QSB_SHORT_CARRY, the switch that selects that square.
added_multiply_lane_stack: QSB_MUL_XMERGE64 / QSB_MUL_LANE64 / QSB_MUL_FOLD64 in GPUMath.h: the live field multiply merges its 512-bit cross-product sum in the eight 64-bit lanes the even column chain already occupies (result lands directly in the fold's r0..r3/h0..h3), merges the two 977 fold chains in four lane adds, and adds the 65-bit top fold as a lane pair that propagates its residual carry one lane further than the 32-bit tail it replaces. Each arm is exact (a lane is a word pair; the inter-lane carry is the carry out of the odd word) and restores the schedule it replaces byte for byte at =0.
added_fold_tail_window: QSB_MUL_FOLDT2 / QSB_SQL_FOLDT2 / QSB_SAS_FOLDT2 / QSB_SAS_K3T1 in GPUMath.h: four independently switched, provably exact narrowings of tails that the 64-bit lane forms of this tree carry further than the build's own declared truncation policy. The three FOLDT2 arms end the lane top fold of the live multiply, the live short-carry square and the fused square-add-subtract after lane 1. Those folds add z8*(2^32+977) as a 65-bit pair -- low 64 bits 977*z8 + (z8<<32) in lane 0, the 65th bit in lane 1 -- and then spent one further instruction propagating the residual carry into lane 2, i.e. words 4 and 5, three words beyond the word-3 terminator of the 32-bit tails the lane forms replaced. The dropped step is reached only when the 65th bit is set and the receiving lane is all ones: the bit needs z8 >= 2^32-976 (below 2^-22.1 for a field-random quotient limb) and the lane needs 2^-64, so the arms differ from the retained form with probability below 2^-86 per reduction, nine orders below the 2^-31 fold exposure QSB_C31 already ships behind the exact host publication gate and below the 2^-63 QSB_CARRY62 tails of the carry-complete build. QSB_SAS_K3T1 subtracts the split-3p constant 3K = 0x3_00000B73 through 64 bits in the fused routine's lane tail, which is exactly the window QSB_C31 declares for the word form this build otherwise selects (differ iff the accumulator's low 64 bits are below 3K, ~2^-30.4); the lane form had been carrying that borrow one lane further only because a lane pair was its cheapest unit. Ten instructions per point addition come out of the multiply alone. Each arm restores its step byte for byte at =0 and is inert wherever its lane fold is.
